goal: Raise the SDK turn cap default from 40 to 500 in both the workflow CLI and task-worker.sh so it acts as a runaway backstop instead of silently undercutting per-task transcript budgets.

references: src/flywheel/workflow.py:74 -- DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS constant; flows into ClaudeAgentOptions(max_turns=...) at workflow.py:297-302
.workflow/task-worker.sh:25 -- MAX_TURNS shell default mirrored to workflow CLI's --max-turns flag; help text at line 61 currently reads 'Max agent turns per attempt (default: 40)'
constraints: Set DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 500 in src/flywheel/workflow.py; do not introduce a config override or env var.
Set MAX_TURNS=500 in .workflow/task-worker.sh and update the --help text so it both states the new default and frames it as a runaway-prevention backstop (not a per-task budget).
If the workflow CLI's argparse help string for --max-turns mentions the default, update it consistently; otherwise leave it untouched.
Do not change DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES, the _AGENT_ALLOWED_TOOLS list, or any invoker behavior.
Run `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` on src/flywheel/workflow.py before reporting verify.
Commit the change with a Conventional Commits message (e.g. 'chore:' or 'fix:') before reporting verify.
non_goals: Do not add a configurable backstop, env var, or per-task override beyond the existing --max-turns flag.
Do not edit any task JSON or any test that pins max_turns to a small value for fast scripted-invoker runs.
edge_cases: Tests that construct HarnessConfig with their own max_turns must continue to pass unchanged -- the default constant only applies when callers do not specify.
task-worker.sh `MAX_TURNS=40` appears twice if someone copy-pasted it; grep for stragglers.

graders.run: uv run python -c "from flywheel.workflow import DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS; assert DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS == 500, DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS"
graders.name: workflow-default
